rawDiagnostics.message: export const dynamic = "force-dynamic" with no visible request-time dependency in this file.
rawDiagnostics.remediation: Remove the force-dynamic export and let Next.js statically render/cache the route, unless the route genuinely needs per-request data (cookies, headers, draftMode, or an explicitly uncached fetch) -- in which case keep it and document why. Evidence: Next.js official documentation on route segment config ("If you prefer your page to always be dynamic... your page won't attempt to be statically generated" -- legitimate uses include dashboards/authenticated content that read per-request context, per Next.js community and official guidance on the dynamic route segment option).

rawDiagnostics.ruleName: Accessible Name Must Contain Visible Label Text
rawDiagnostics.message: Accessible name (aria-label) does not contain the element's visible text label (WCAG 2.5.3).
rawDiagnostics.remediation: Include the element's visible text as a substring of its aria-label, or remove the redundant aria-label if the visible text alone is already an adequate accessible name. Evidence: W3C WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 2.5.3 "Label in Name" (Level A) -- https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/label-in-name.html.

rawDiagnostics.ruleName: Effect Used Solely to Derive State
rawDiagnostics.message: useEffect body consists solely of a state-setter call; this derived value can be computed during render instead.
rawDiagnostics.remediation: Delete the Effect and the corresponding state variable; compute the value directly in the component body during render (wrap in useMemo only if the computation is measurably expensive). Evidence: React official documentation, "You Might Not Need an Effect" -- https://react.dev/learn/you-might-not-need-an-effect ("If there is no external system involved... you shouldn't need an Effect").

rawDiagnostics.ruleName: Missing Reactive Dependency in Effect Hook
rawDiagnostics.message: useEffect reads a component prop that is missing from its dependency array.
rawDiagnostics.remediation: Add the missing prop to the Effect's dependency array. Evidence: React official documentation, useEffect reference, "Specifying reactive dependencies" -- https://react.dev/reference/react/useEffect#specifying-reactive-dependencies ("Your Effect's dependencies... must include every reactive value you read in the Effect").
